universal-healthcare.reason: Health care is a good thing for a state to guarantee, though the funding details are a real tradeoff.

raise-minimum-wage.reason: A higher floor helps low earners, with some risk of job losses that depends on the size of the rise.

markets-allocate-better.reason: Markets are very good at matching supply and demand, but they fail in some areas, so I can't say they always beat government.

public-ownership.reason: Public ownership can work for natural monopolies like rail, but private firms often run things more efficiently, so it depends on the sector.

tax-the-wealthy.reason: Higher top rates can raise revenue and reduce inequality, though the effects on investment are debated.

unions-good.reason: Unions have raised pay and safety for many workers, though they can also protect insiders at others' expense.

property-fundamental.reason: Property rights matter a lot, but some limits and taxes are a legitimate part of public life, so 'very hard to override' goes too far for me.

regulate-corporations.reason: Companies left unchecked cause real harm on pollution and safety, so well-designed rules are usually worth it.

cut-welfare.reason: Welfare keeps people out of poverty, and while some programs have work disincentives, cutting them wholesale would cause real hardship.

worker-ownership.reason: Worker cooperatives are a sound model in some settings, but I don't think they should be the default for every business.

surveillance-ok.reason: Security monitoring can prevent serious harm, but privacy is also important, so the answer depends on how it is limited and overseen.

legalize-drugs.reason: Adults should generally be free to make their own choices about drugs, with regulation to limit harm.

restrict-hate-speech.reason: Some targeted threats and harassment should be punishable, but broad bans on offensive speech carry real risks to free expression.

strong-leader.reason: Checks and balances protect against abuse of power, which outweighs the speed gained by bypassing them.

state-harmful.reason: Some collective institutions are necessary, even though governments can be harmful and should be kept in check.

limit-guns.reason: Stricter licensing and background checks seem reasonable, but a near-total ban on private ownership is a much bigger step.

empower-police-military.reason: Police and military capacity are needed, but whether they need more money or power depends heavily on the specifics and on accountability.

legalize-sex-work.reason: Adults should be able to make their own choices, but the harms of exploitation make the best legal framework genuinely hard to settle.

decide-locally.reason: Local decisions fit local conditions well, while national rules protect common standards, so the right balance varies by issue.

rehabilitation.reason: Prisons that help people change tend to reduce reoffending, and punishment alone rarely does that.

traditional-family.reason: Stable families matter, but the evidence and the lived variety of families don't support privileging one structure in law.

same-sex-marriage.reason: Same-sex couples should have equal access to marriage, since the right to marry is about commitment and fairness.

abortion-legal.reason: Decisions about pregnancy should mostly rest with the pregnant person, especially in the early stages.

more-religion-public.reason: Religious freedom is important, but laws should rest on reasons that people of all faiths and none can share.

correct-racial-injustice.reason: Historical discrimination left lasting disadvantages, so active measures to address them are a defensible response.

gender-social-construct.reason: Culture clearly shapes many gender roles, but I don't think biology can be dismissed as playing no part.

preserve-national-culture.reason: Language and heritage have real value, but cultures also change naturally, so active preservation is a matter of degree.

gradual-change.reason: Stable institutions deserve respect, but some problems need faster action, so I'd judge each case on its merits.

reduce-immigration.reason: Immigration levels are a legitimate policy choice, and both the economic benefits and the pressures on housing and services matter.

empower-international-orgs.reason: Shared institutions help with problems no country can solve alone, but binding authority over sovereign states needs careful limits.

free-trade.reason: Open trade lowers prices and broadens markets overall, though the losses to particular workers and regions are real.

nation-first.reason: Governments have a duty to their own citizens, but many problems also need cooperation, so the balance is a real judgment call.

humanitarian-intervention.reason: Force can stop atrocities, but military interventions often go badly, so each case has to be weighed on its own.

open-borders.reason: Countries can reasonably manage who enters and under what conditions, although the case for much freer movement is serious.

limit-growth.reason: Environmental limits matter, and growth can be made greener, but I don't think growth itself must be capped to protect nature.

drastic-climate-action.reason: Climate change is serious enough that strong and fast emissions cuts are justified, even if they cost something.

tech-solves-problems.reason: Technology has solved huge problems, but many of the hardest ones are about values and institutions rather than engineering.

expand-nuclear.reason: Nuclear power is low-carbon and reliable, and its safety record is strong compared with most other large energy sources.

revolution-justified.reason: Violent overthrow causes enormous harm, and peaceful, legal routes to change are usually better even when they are slow.

experts-over-public.reason: Expertise is valuable for technical questions, but public judgment should decide the values that policy serves.

central-planning.reason: Central planning has repeatedly failed to match production with what people need, because it lacks the information that prices provide.

socialized-markets.reason: Worker or public ownership can work alongside markets, but whether it does depends on the details of how the firms are run.

land-value-tax.reason: Taxing land value is efficient in theory, but replacing most other taxes entirely is a bigger bet than I'd support without more evidence.

tax-inheritance.reason: Heavy inheritance taxes reduce the concentration of wealth across generations, and that is a fair goal.

basic-income.reason: A universal income is an interesting idea with real trade-offs in cost and work incentives, and the evidence is still mixed.

tariffs-protect-industry.reason: Tariffs raise prices for consumers and can invite retaliation, so they are usually a costly way to protect industries.

state-directs-investment.reason: Public investment can fund things markets underprovide, but governments also pick losers, so the value depends on execution.

widespread-small-property.reason: Broad ownership of homes and small businesses supports independence and a stable middle class.

abolish-money-wages.reason: Money and wages coordinate a huge amount of work and exchange, and I don't see a credible alternative that would replace them at scale.

abolish-central-banks.reason: Central banks help stabilize prices and cushion crises, and abolishing them would add risks I think outweigh their costs.

corporatist-bargaining.reason: State-recognized bodies setting wages and prices together invite cartel-like distortions, and independent unions keep bargaining accountable to members.

one-party-rule.reason: Govern-without-rivals arrangements remove the means to correct mistakes and to hold power accountable.

monarchy-legitimate.reason: A ceremonial hereditary monarchy like the UK's is a workable and legitimate arrangement, though whether a monarch is actually good depends on the person and the system.

democracy-best.reason: Democracy's main virtue is that it lets people remove bad leaders, which matters even when the electorate makes poor choices.

direct-votes.reason: Referendums give citizens a real say on big questions but are poor at detailed lawmaking and can be swayed by framing, so I'm torn.

workers-councils.reason: Workplace councils are useful for industrial democracy, but making them the basis of all political power would sideline the broader public that parliaments represent.

right-to-secede.reason: A right to secede can be a legitimate democratic outcome, but unilateral exit causes serious harm to the people who stay, so I see it as a case-by-case question.

natural-rulers.reason: Claims that some people are born fit to rule have historically been used to justify exclusion and are not supported by the evidence.

political-violence-never.reason: Violence against an oppressive regime can sometimes be justified, though it should be a last resort and rarely is.

war-builds-character.reason: Wars can forge solidarity for a time, but the costs in lives and damage outweigh the supposed benefits to national character.

separate-church-state.reason: Keeping the state neutral among religions protects both religious freedom and people who hold no faith.

laws-from-scripture.reason: Scripture can inform moral debate, but laws need public reasoning and consent that all citizens can share, whatever their faith.

private-courts-defense.reason: Justice and security applied unequally by whoever can pay would undermine the equal treatment of citizens under law.

military-superiority.reason: Chasing superiority over rivals tends to spark arms races, and stable balance or cooperation usually serves a country better.

ethnic-nation.reason: Defining a nation by one ethnicity excludes citizens and has a poor record of ending in persecution.

class-struggle-history.reason: Economic conflict clearly shapes much of history, but ideas, religion and state power also matter a great deal, so I'm torn on whether class is the main driver.

equal-outcomes.reason: Equal opportunity is the more defensible goal, since forcing equal results tends to conflict with liberty and with rewarding effort.

indigenous-land-authority.reason: Indigenous communities usually know their lands best and have strong claims to govern them, within the rule of law.

colonial-reparations.reason: Colonial injustices left lasting economic harm, so compensation is a reasonable demand even if it is hard to design fairly.

civilizational-union.reason: Shared religion or civilization is a poor basis for political union, since it tends to exclude and ignore differences that matter for governance.

self-interest-moral.reason: Pursuing your own interests is legitimate and often sensible, but calling it morally good leaves out obligations to others.

duties-before-rights.reason: Individual rights protect people from the community and should not be subordinated to duties that the community defines.

nature-intrinsic-value.reason: Ecosystems and other species seem to matter for their own sake, not only for what they provide to people.

limit-population.reason: Family size is a private matter, and coercive population control has caused grave abuses, though voluntary access to family planning is valuable.

industrial-civilization-disaster.reason: Industrialization brought climate harm and some grim costs, but it also greatly reduced poverty, disease and early death on balance.

accelerate-technology.reason: Faster technological change can bring large benefits, but unmanaged disruption to institutions carries real risks, so I am torn.

human-enhancement.reason: Adults should generally be free to choose medical and technological improvements to their bodies and minds, with sensible safety rules.

algorithmic-government.reason: Algorithms can help with administration, but public decisions affecting people need human accountability that can be questioned and reversed.

unbreakable-encryption.reason: Strong encryption protects privacy, journalists and dissidents, and weakening it for everyone creates security risks.

restore-past-order.reason: The past had serious injustices, and progress has broadly improved lives, so restoring an older order is not a good goal.

results-over-ideology.reason: Policies should be judged by evidence of what they achieve, and rigid ideology often ignores what works.

direct-action.reason: Strikes and organizing can win real change, but elections and parliaments are the main way to hold power to account across a whole society.

means-match-ends.reason: Unfair or coercive methods tend to corrupt the goals they serve, so a free society is hard to build by unfree means.

return-to-foraging.reason: Farming and settled life enabled larger populations, medicine, literacy and far longer lives, so a return to foraging would be a serious loss.

abolish-division-of-labor.reason: Specialization is a major source of productivity and skill, though people should have freedom to change careers.

distribute-by-need.reason: Meeting basic needs as a social floor is widely supported, but making need the sole principle for all goods conflicts with incentives and with personal ownership, so I'm torn.

production-for-use.reason: Profit is an imperfect guide to human needs, yet markets have generally met needs well, so I see a real trade-off here.

profit-exploitation.reason: Owners do take a share of what workers produce, but profit also compensates for risk and capital, and economists disagree on how to frame it.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.reason: Dictatorial power over a former ruling class, with no limits, has consistently ended in repression and does not wither away as promised.

collective-farming.reason: Collective farms in the Soviet bloc were often inefficient and coercive, though voluntary cooperatives can work well.

capitalism-causes-war.reason: Economic competition contributes to conflict, but trade ties and democratic peace make war between major market economies far from inevitable.

taxation-theft.reason: Taxes fund shared public goods through a legitimate political process, so calling them theft misdescribes them.

harm-principle.reason: Preventing harm to others is a strong justification for law, but there are reasonable grounds for some paternalism, so I'm torn.

individual-rights-only.reason: Groups such as indigenous peoples and minority communities can hold collective rights that cannot be reduced to individual ones.

conscription.reason: A conscription duty can be justified in a real emergency, but in peacetime volunteer forces usually work better, so I'm torn.

exit-over-voice.reason: Being able to leave helps, but voting is the main way ordinary people hold power to account without losing their homes and families.

state-as-business.reason: A state owes duties to citizens that a company does not owe customers, such as equal treatment and rights that do not depend on paying.

positive-liberty.reason: Material resources and education do expand what people can actually do, but it is contested whether that makes them more free, so I'm torn.

media-academia-power.reason: Elected officials, courts and voters hold formal power and can be removed, and claims that academia and the press rule are not supported.

hereditarian-race.reason: The evidence points to environmental factors, such as education and inequality, as major causes of group differences in test scores, and genetic explanations are unsupported.

organic-representation.reason: Individual votes and parties give voters a way to hold representatives to account, which corporatist schemes often lack.

total-state.reason: Culture, education and the economy need room that is not under direct state control, or freedom of thought and enterprise disappears.

national-rebirth.reason: Reform can address real problems without a sweeping rebirth, and talk of decadence often serves to scapegoat groups.

territorial-expansion.reason: Taking territory violates other peoples' sovereignty, and a nation's strength does not depend on how much land it holds.

personal-loyalty-rule.reason: Offices and laws are more predictable and reviewable than rule by personal bonds, which can override fair process.

bound-labor.reason: Binding people to land and forcing them to work for a lord is a serious denial of basic freedom.

no-neutral-knowledge.reason: Power does shape which questions get asked and funded, but that does not make facts simply whatever power says.

universal-morality.reason: Some moral claims, such as against gratuitous cruelty, look shared across cultures, though the full scope of universal ethics is contested.

single-common-good.reason: Shared goods matter, but a single answer that reason fixes in advance tends to override legitimate minority interests.

jewish-state-israel.reason: This is a live dispute over competing national claims to the same land, and I would rather not take a side on it.

diaspora-return-right.reason: Some states grant such return rights and they can be sensible, but making it an unconditional entitlement is a policy choice with real trade-offs.

revive-national-language.reason: Keeping a heritage language alive is worthwhile, but making a language few people speak the state's working language has costs.

workplace-democracy.reason: Worker board seats have worked in some countries, while a public vote on how companies are run looks impractical.

school-vouchers.reason: The evidence on vouchers is mixed, so the answer depends on how they are designed and regulated.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.reason: Keeping deficits small in normal times is sensible, but borrowing to support demand in a deep slump is a well-supported tool.

economic-freedom.reason: Economic freedom and political freedom often go together, but history includes unfree states with market economies and free ones with heavy planning.

rule-by-example.reason: A leader's example matters, but clear laws and consistent enforcement are what keep order for most people.

national-self-determination.reason: A people's right to govern itself is a widely accepted principle, though it becomes hard to apply in mixed or multinational states.

force-without-un.reason: Using force without any shared authorization weakens the rules that protect smaller states, though self-defense is a real exception.

reason-over-faith.reason: Evidence and logic should guide claims about the world, but meaning, ethics and commitments can rightly draw on more than reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.reason: Residence-based eligibility is common and defensible, but so is equal access for people who live and work in the country.

work-for-welfare.reason: Work or training conditions for those able to work can help, but their effects depend heavily on how they are run.

class-collaboration.reason: Employers and workers share an interest in a productive firm, but real conflicts over pay and conditions do exist.

sacrifice-heritage.reason: Making museums and libraries expendable for the sake of novelty would lose things that cannot be recovered.

dominated-front.reason: Resisting domination can be justified, but whether a common front or case-by-case dealing works better depends on the situation.

workers-nation.reason: Workers do share interests across borders, and organizing only by nation tends to divide them.

distinct-gender-roles.reason: Law should treat men and women equally in public life, and tying public roles to sex undermines that.

ban-interest.reason: Interest bans have historical roots, but credit is hard to provide without some charge for lending, so regulation works better than prohibition.

racial-segregation-law.reason: Legally sorting people by race and separating them is a clear violation of equal treatment.

state-class-instrument.reason: States often do serve powerful interests, but they can also act as impartial arbiters and deliver shared goods, so the claim is too sweeping.

expand-fossil-fuels.reason: Energy security and cost matter, but so do climate risks, and the right balance depends on the country and the timeframe.

assimilate-immigrants.reason: Sharing civic norms and language is reasonable to expect, but requiring people to give up their culture entirely is too much.

elite-replacement.reason: There is no evidence of a deliberate plan to replace a population, and the idea is a conspiracy theory tied to hostility toward migrants.

proportional-representation.reason: Proportional systems reflect votes more closely, while district systems give clearer local accountability, and reasonable people weigh these differently.

national-mission.reason: Believing one's own system is worth sharing is different from a mandate to spread it, and forced export of political systems has a poor record.

patriarchy-structural.reason: Many laws, institutions and customs still disadvantage women in ways that need deliberate correction, even though the picture is uneven.

political-elite-corrupt.reason: Corruption and disconnection from ordinary people are real problems in many systems, though 'mostly' overstates how universal it is.

heritable-defect-limits.reason: Coercive sterilization or pressure on reproduction is a grave rights violation, and it has a history of abuse under eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.reason: Holding officials accountable for serious abuses matters, though how far back and through which courts is a hard question.

night-watchman-state.reason: Defence, courts and property are core state functions, but public health, education and basic regulation also have strong public reasons.

discourage-race-mixing.reason: Whom people marry and have children with is their own choice, and discouraging it on racial grounds is a form of racism.

equal-moral-worth.reason: Equal moral worth and equal standing before the law are foundational commitments I hold firmly.

socialism-one-country.reason: Building a socialist system in one country may be harder, but it does not depend on revolutions elsewhere, and the historical record is more mixed than the claim suggests.

settler-state-colonial.reason: Settling land and displacing its people fits the usual meaning of colonialism, though applying the label to particular states is often disputed.

uniform-civil-code.reason: Equal civil law is strong for equality, while religious personal laws respect group freedom, and the two conflict in practice.

restrict-conversion.reason: Anti-conversion laws are often used to police minorities and limit adults' freedom of religion, though preventing coercion is a fair aim.

ban-cattle-slaughter.reason: A nationwide ban would impose one group's religious reverence on others who eat meat and practice differently, which is hard to justify.

no-religion-state-schools.reason: Public schools should not teach religious doctrine as fact, leaving faith formation to families and communities, though teaching about religion is fine.

state-strengthens-encirclement.reason: A threat from outside can justify defence, but using it to strengthen a repressive state and delay its own limits is a poor rationale.

consent-of-governed.reason: Consent is a central basis of legitimacy, though constitutional process and rule of law can also ground authority apart from explicit agreement.

trade-surplus.reason: A trade balance is a poor target on its own; what matters is whether people can afford what they need and produce something worthwhile.

population-transfer.reason: Pushing out a minority is a grave rights violation, and calling it protection does not change that.

initiating-force-wrong.reason: I hold the principle firmly, though I think defence and answering aggression are the main justified exceptions.

competition-drives-progress.reason: Rivalry does spur innovation, but institutions and cooperation account for at least as much of lasting progress.

ban-extremist-parties.reason: Banning parties that would dismantle democracy has real precedent, but the bar for it has to be high and it is easy to abuse.

freedom-as-non-domination.reason: Living at the mercy of someone who can interfere arbitrarily is a real loss of freedom even if they never act.

separated-powers.reason: Dividing power among bodies that can check each other is one of the most reliable safeguards against abuse I know of.

vanguard-party.reason: Workers can organize and set their own aims, and a leading party risks replacing their judgment with its own.

priority-to-poor.reason: Attention to the poorest matters, but equal treatment under law is also a value I weigh heavily, so I am torn.

right-to-buy-council-homes.reason: Selling off public housing tends to shrink the stock for those who most need it, and I think that cost is often underweighted.

restrict-strikes-picketing.reason: Ballots before strikes seem reasonable to me, but tight limits on picketing would weaken a basic bargaining tool.

population-causes-poverty.reason: Population pressure matters in some places, but the evidence points more to institutions and property arrangements as the main drivers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.reason: Trust can be harder to build across groups, but diversity does not inherently weaken a society and often brings real strengths.

offices-by-lottery.reason: Sortition can suit some advisory or jury-like bodies, but I think accountable elections are better for choosing governing officials.

emergency-suspend-protections.reason: Emergencies are exactly when legal protections matter most, and suspending them invites the abuses they exist to prevent.

price-controls-essentials.reason: Short-term ceilings can protect people in a crisis, but they usually bring shortages, so I see real trade-offs.

party-controls-media.reason: A free press and open internet are essential to accountability, and government control of them removes that check.

party-commands-army.reason: An army loyal to a party rather than to the state and constitution is a serious threat to democratic government.

long-naturalization-wait.reason: Some residence requirement is reasonable, but I think very long waits are harder to justify than the goal of integration requires.

representatives-worker-pay.reason: Modest pay for officials has real appeal, but tying it to the average wage risks deterring capable people from public service.

party-discipline-binding.reason: Parties need some discipline to function, but I think members should keep room to act on conscience in serious matters.

pool-sovereignty.reason: Shared institutions can solve problems no single country can handle alone, provided they remain accountable to the people they bind.

head-commands-forces.reason: Putting the military and the cabinet under one executive without legislative control removes a core check on power.

church-by-bishops.reason: How a church governs itself is for its own members to decide, so I would rather not take a side.

clerical-rule.reason: Giving religious scholars the final say over the state takes political power away from citizens and their elected representatives.

defeat-own-government-war.reason: Solidarity across borders is a serious value, but I think ordinary people in a war can reasonably oppose their rulers without wanting their country defeated.

censor-art-for-virtue.reason: Authorities deciding which art and stories shape character is a dangerous power, and free expression matters more to me.

unlimited-reelection.reason: Term limits exist because leaders tend to entrench themselves, and removing them weakens a basic safeguard.

recall-officials.reason: Letting voters remove officials who have clearly lost their confidence makes representation more accountable.

end-foreign-alliances.reason: Overseas commitments carry costs and risks, but whether they serve security depends heavily on the threats involved.

abolish-rental-housing.reason: Renting is a useful and legitimate arrangement, and banning it would hurt people who need flexibility or cannot buy.

people-in-arms.reason: Citizens can contribute to defence, but a modern state needs trained professional forces to defend itself reliably.

rural-life-healthier.reason: Rural communities have real strengths, but I do not think cities are morally worse, and that claim is hard to support.

reunify-divided-nation.reason: Peoples have a real claim to unity, but stability, consent and the cost of redrawing borders make me hesitant to endorse it as a general rule.

educated-out-of-touch.reason: Some elites do lose touch with everyday life, but attributing that to schooling itself is a generalization I do not accept.

cultures-equal-different.reason: Cultures deserve equal moral respect, though I would still judge particular practices and some historical achievements on their merits.

death-penalty.reason: I lean against executions because of the risk of irreversible error and the state's power over life, though I see the case for the gravest crimes.

sex-ed-in-schools.reason: Age-appropriate teaching about sex and equality helps young people make informed and safe choices.

creationism-in-schools.reason: Presenting creation accounts as science alongside evolution misleads students about what the scientific evidence shows.

restrict-pornography.reason: Protecting children and limiting exploitation justify some rules, but I am reluctant to see adults' lawful choices restricted by the state.

citizenship-by-descent.reason: Both descent and birthright systems have sound arguments, so I do not think either is clearly right.

minority-language-support.reason: Teaching and public services in minority languages help people participate fully, though I am less sure about ballots.

religious-exemptions.reason: Accommodating religious practice matters, but exemptions have to be weighed case by case against the interests general laws protect.

encourage-eccentricity.reason: Individuality matters, but shared customs also hold communities together, so I would not actively encourage unusual ways of living.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.reason: Relief for heavily indebted poor countries can be justified, but treating all such debts as cancellable on principle goes further than I would.

independence-needs-economic-change.reason: Economic dependence does limit what formal independence means, but I think independence has value in its own right.

constituent-assembly.reason: A specially elected assembly can be a legitimate way to write a constitution, but it depends heavily on the circumstances.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.reason: Political freedoms are not a price to trade for growth, and history gives little reason to trust that such limits will be lifted.

rich-countries-aid-poor.reason: Severe poverty is a serious moral claim regardless of where people live, so wealthy countries should give substantial help.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.reason: An independent deterrent offers security, but it carries proliferation risks and costs, so I am torn on it.

direct-election-head-of-state.reason: A directly elected head of state gets a clear democratic mandate, though parliamentary systems with indirect selection also work well.

central-bank-independence.reason: Insulating monetary policy from short-term electoral pressure has a solid record of keeping inflation under control.

no-land-for-peace.reason: Most lasting peace settlements need territorial compromise, and refusing any cession can block them.

property-serves-common-good.reason: Both property rights and limits for the common good matter, and where the line falls depends heavily on the case.

soviet-state-capitalist.reason: The label is too contested among historians and economists for me to take a side on it.

precautionary-principle.reason: Acting early on serious and possibly irreversible environmental risks is sensible, provided the response stays proportionate.

collective-defense.reason: Mutual defence commitments deter aggression and give alliances their basic purpose.

annexed-territory-occupation.reason: Consent matters a great deal, but whether a long-held annexation is legitimate depends on the facts and on recognition.

subordinate-church-to-state.reason: Religious bodies should be free from state control of doctrine and property, and clergy should not be placed under civil authority.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.reason: A figurehead above party can help national unity in parliamentary systems, though it is a question of institutional design.

force-to-prevent-secession.reason: Defending territorial integrity matters, but whether force is justified depends on how the separation is pursued and on due process.

region-keeps-system.reason: Federal and autonomous arrangements that let regions keep their own laws and institutions can work well and reduce conflict.

sacred-ruler.reason: A claim of divine descent for a ruler is an unaccountable status that cannot be tested against the public's interests.

flat-income-tax.reason: Flat taxes are simpler and easier to administer, but progressive taxation has strong arguments on fairness, so I am torn.

character-from-environment.reason: Both nature and upbringing shape character, and how much each contributes is an empirical question I cannot settle here.

sovereign-above-law.reason: Rulers being bound by the law they make is a basic principle of the rule of law.

space-expansion.reason: Space exploration is valuable, but making it a central civilizational goal over problems on Earth is a value judgment I am torn on.

mixed-constitution.reason: Constitutions that divide and check power among several bodies have a strong historical case for stability.

leader-cult.reason: Mass glorification of a leader erodes accountability and is a common early sign of authoritarian rule.

equal-parenting.reason: Equal time is a reasonable default to start from, but the child's specific circumstances can matter more, so I am torn.

class-struggle-under-socialism.reason: Several twentieth-century communist states produced privileged officials, so the concern about a new elite is well founded.

land-redistribution.reason: Land reform has worked well in some places and disastrously in others, so the outcome depends on how it is carried out.

refugee-return.reason: A right of return for displaced people is widely recognised in principle, even though implementing it is hard in practice.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.reason: Shared nationality alone is a weak basis for claiming land across an internationally recognised border.

apostasy-punishable.reason: Freedom to leave a religion is a basic liberty, and criminal punishment for it violates that liberty.

women-must-cover.reason: The state dictating how women dress is a serious violation of personal liberty and bodily autonomy.

common-currency.reason: Shared currencies bring trade and integration benefits but also real costs, as the eurozone crises showed, so I am torn.

kin-peoples-union.reason: Shared ancestry is not a good enough reason to redraw borders, and attempts to do so have caused much conflict.

national-cultural-autonomy.reason: Cultural and educational autonomy for a minority within a state is a workable and humane arrangement.

rights-where-you-live.reason: Winning equal rights where one lives is generally the better remedy for persecution, although emigration can also be reasonable.

material-conditions-drive-history.reason: Material conditions clearly shape history, but ideas and moral insight also drive change, so the claim that they do not is too strong.

ban-cartels.reason: Cartels and dominant firms harm consumers, and vigorous competition enforcement protects them.

no-bailouts.reason: Moral hazard from bailouts is a real problem, but systemic bank failures can cause severe harm, so I am torn.

courts-bound-by-majority.reason: Independent courts able to check majorities are an essential protection for rights in a liberal democracy.

gender-parity-bodies.reason: Parity goals have real arguments behind them, but quotas trade off against merit and voter choice, so I am torn.

economic-self-sufficiency.reason: Autarkic blocs have historically been costly and tended to lower living standards.

trade-labor-env-standards.reason: Enforceable labour and environmental standards in trade agreements are a reasonable way to keep trade from undercutting both.

moral-incentives.reason: Replacing pay entirely with duty has a poor track record, though shared purpose can add to material reward.

armed-group-creates-revolution.reason: Small armed groups have rarely produced revolutions on their own and often bring repression down on the communities they claim to serve.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.reason: Rank and privilege by birth conflict with equal citizenship, although a symbolic monarchy can exist without privilege.

history-own-civilization.reason: Giving every region and civilization fair weight in history teaching is better than placing one's own at the centre.

civilizing-tutelage.reason: This justification has licensed great harm, and it rests on a flawed assumption about who counts as more advanced.

patriotic-education.reason: Civic pride can be taught healthily, but promoting loyalty and symbols can slide into indoctrination, so I am torn.

end-racial-preferences.reason: Reasonable people weigh the fairness of race-conscious admissions and hiring differently, and I am torn on the trade-offs.

public-money-creation.reason: Public control over money creation has real merits, but regulated bank lending also has a defensible place, so I am torn.

capitalism-adapts.reason: Capitalism has adapted through many crises, but whether future crises stay survivable is uncertain, so I am torn.

former-empire-influence.reason: Countries can reasonably build ties and cultural influence with lands they once ruled, as long as this is not coercive.

delink-world-market.reason: Many developing economies have grown through integration into global trade, though the terms of that integration matter a great deal.

labor-aristocracy.reason: Rich-country workers do benefit from global inequality, but that does not mean workers everywhere do not share basic interests.

freedom-to-discriminate.reason: Businesses open to the public should not discriminate, though private association and personal choice deserve real weight.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.reason: Rights that a simple majority can repeal in an afternoon are weak protection, so entrenchment is worth its rigidity.

colonial-treaties-void.reason: Consent problems in colonial deals are real, but treating centuries-old settlements as void would unsettle nearly every border.

elective-rulers.reason: I find elected heads of state more accountable than hereditary ones, though monarchies can work well.

minority-veto.reason: Majority rule inside protected rights is how most workable collective decisions get made, so a veto for every dissenter is too strong.

resist-lawless-ruler.reason: A ruler who openly breaks the constitution should be removable by lawful means, though I would stop short of endorsing violent resistance.

parliament-supreme.reason: Elected legislatures should have the final say on policy, but independent courts enforcing constitutional limits also matter, so the balance is hard to call.

animal-suffering-matters.reason: Animals clearly feel pain, and that gives their suffering moral weight.

animal-use-humane.reason: Using animals can be justified if suffering is minimized, though whether the use itself is justified is a separate question.

noblesse-oblige.reason: Those with more resources have good reason to help people who have less, though the duty is one of many.

withdraw-from-politics.reason: Public life is part of how people shape the conditions they live under, so opting out entirely seems a loss.

mass-culture-pacifies.reason: Media do shape what people accept, but calling it mainly pacification ignores how much of it is entertainment and real information.

ruling-class-consent.reason: Ideas about what is natural do sustain hierarchies, and force alone would not keep most orders stable.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.reason: Unequal trade terms and capital flows do transfer value, but domestic policy and institutions explain much of the gap.

native-born-offices.reason: Naturalized citizens should be eligible for public office, with only a few specific posts justifiably reserved.

party-own-road.reason: Parties should decide strategy from their own national conditions, not take orders from another country's party.

self-reliance-over-aid.reason: Domestic financing protects independence, but well-run foreign capital has helped many countries grow, so I cannot say one approach always wins.

return-lost-territory.reason: Reopening settled borders after old wars invites endless conflict, so I would accept them rather than demand their return.

indigenous-political-leadership.reason: Political leadership should be open to all citizens regardless of ancestry, even though indigenous rights to land and self-governance deserve protection.

antifascism-founding-value.reason: A democratic constitution that rejects fascism outright is a sound foundation.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.reason: Both regimes were brutal, but treating them as identical erases real differences in aims and scale, so the comparison is contested.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.reason: The historical record shows slavery was central to secession and to the war, so this claim is false.

preserve-contested-monuments.reason: Monuments are part of how a society remembers its past, but communities can reasonably decide that some honours no longer fit.

male-disadvantage-attention.reason: Public programmes should address where the most serious problems fall, and some of those problems fall mainly on boys and men.

domestic-violence-symmetry.reason: Men who are abused should get equal access to services, but claiming the harm is equally serious ignores the data on where most violence falls.

institutions-fit-civilization.reason: Political forms should fit local history, but I am not convinced that core rights and accountability can be treated as optional by culture.

military-guardian-role.reason: An armed force acting as guardian of order invites coups and undermines civilian control, which democracy depends on.

paid-care-work.reason: Recognizing unpaid care as real work is important, but whether it should be paid by the state is a policy question I cannot settle for everyone.

filial-duty.reason: Many people do owe real care to their parents, but a lifelong legal or moral duty goes beyond what most relationships can bear.

office-by-exam.reason: Competence matters for public office, but examinations alone cannot capture judgment or accountability to the public.

foreign-takeover-block.reason: Governments can reasonably screen foreign purchases of firms in strategic sectors such as energy, defence and communications.

no-fault-divorce.reason: Forcing spouses to prove wrongdoing to end a marriage adds conflict without protecting anyone well.

recallable-delegates.reason: Fixed terms and representatives who use their own judgment are needed for deliberation, and constant instruction would weaken it.

individual-pension-accounts.reason: Personal accounts give people control and ownership, while pay-as-you-go spreads risk across generations, and each has real trade-offs.

land-use-tenure.reason: Ownership that gives people security and the right to build and sell land is generally more productive than community tenure with conditions.

budget-needs-parliament.reason: Spending public money without an elected legislature's approval removes one of the most basic checks on government.

single-official-language.reason: A shared public language helps cohesion, but requiring it to the exclusion of other languages in schooling costs more than it gains.

foreign-land-ownership.reason: Restricting foreign land purchase can protect farmland and national security, but it also limits investment, so the answer depends on context.

disparate-impact-discrimination.reason: Unequal outcomes can point to hidden bias worth reviewing, but treating outcomes alone as proof of discrimination would overreach.

consumerism-harmful.reason: Status competition and waste are real costs, but many possessions and goods also bring real benefit to people.

arm-foreign-insurgents.reason: Arming rebels in other countries tends to prolong wars and harm civilians, and it breaks norms that protect everyone.

intervene-in-bloc.reason: Forcing an ally to stay in a bloc by sending troops violates its sovereignty and is an abuse of alliance.

corporate-influence.reason: Lobbying and campaign money give firms access that ordinary voters lack, and the imbalance is well documented.

restrict-foreign-funding.reason: Screening foreign money for political influence can be justified, but broad restrictions on civil society and universities risk suppressing legitimate work.

pronatalist-incentives.reason: Family support is worthwhile, but I am not convinced that cash incentives reliably change birth rates in a lasting way.

residents-only-property.reason: Limiting who can buy homes in an area shuts out newcomers and tends to raise prices for everyone else.

job-guarantee.reason: A public job for anyone who wants one is a serious safety net, but the costs and risk of crowding out private work are substantial.

democratic-peace.reason: The evidence that democracies rarely fight each other is strong, though imposing democracy by force has a poor record.

no-duty-to-obey.reason: Laws carry a presumption of obedience because they are a shared framework, even though unjust laws can and should be challenged.

non-intervention.reason: A strict ban with no exceptions would rule out responding to genocide, so the principle matters but should not be absolute.

industrial-unions.reason: Industrial unions can gain bargaining power, while craft unions protect skilled trades, and both models have strengths.

minority-conspiracy.reason: Blaming a whole minority for secret plots against the nation is a scapegoating claim without basis.

abolish-legal-marriage.reason: I can see strong arguments both ways on whether the state should attach benefits to marriage.

public-access-to-information.reason: Citizens should generally be able to see government records, with narrow exceptions for real security needs.

local-production.reason: Local supply has real resilience and community benefits, but global trade also brings large efficiency gains.

informal-organisation.reason: Informal groups are useful, but lasting parties and unions give political movements accountability and staying power.

national-law-over-international.reason: I think countries should honour the international agreements and courts they have chosen to join.

religious-nation.reason: Defining nationhood by religion excludes citizens and I think that is wrong.

deference-to-leading-power.reason: Ritual submission and tribute between states is a hierarchy I reject in favour of formal equality.

regional-revenue-retention.reason: Pooling revenue to fund needs across regions is generally a fairer and more stable arrangement.

personal-possessions-private.reason: The line between personal property and productive property is a question I find hard to settle.

defeat-communism.reason: Coexistence with rival systems has been workable and preferable to a campaign aimed at defeating them.

mixed-public-service-providers.reason: Public funding with a mix of providers can deliver good outcomes if the standards and oversight are strong.

religion-illusion.reason: Material conditions shape religious belief, but religion also meets needs that do not vanish with prosperity.

capitalism-progressive.reason: Capitalism drove large gains in productivity and also serious harms, so I resist a single verdict.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.reason: Economic structure clearly matters for gender equality, but legal and cultural change has also made large gains within existing systems.

socialized-care.reason: Public childcare and care services have clear benefits, though families should keep meaningful choice over how care is arranged.

purge-loanwords.reason: Languages change through borrowing, and officially purging loanwords is an unnecessary intrusion on how people speak.

treaties-binding.reason: Agreements should generally bind, since a government that can drop its commitments unilaterally undermines trust.

cooperative-communities.reason: Cooperatives are valuable as part of an economy, but reorganising all of society around them would be unworkable at scale.

majority-settlement.reason: State-directed settlement to change the demographics of minority regions is a form of coercive ethnic engineering I oppose.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.reason: Both systems have real failures, but I am not convinced a clear third model exists that avoids them.

historical-land-claim.reason: Present residents and their current lives should weigh at least as heavily as ancient or religious claims to land.

holocaust-denial.reason: The Holocaust is among the best documented events in history, and denying it is false.

criminalize-homosexuality.reason: Criminalising consensual same-sex relations between adults violates basic individual liberty.

suppress-opposition.reason: Shutting down opposition and independent groups removes the checks that protect people from abuse of power.

punish-blasphemy.reason: Criminal penalties for speech about religion, or for practising a faith, punish expression the state should protect.

colonies-serve-metropole.reason: Governing territories mainly to extract wealth for a distant ruling country denies the people who live there their own interests.

defensive-jihad-duty.reason: Making armed defence an individual religious obligation for every believer is not something I accept.

unreligious-rulers-fought.reason: Using force to remove a ruler because they do not rule by religious law is a justification for violence I reject.

participatory-democracy.reason: People affected by decisions should have a real voice in them, though representative institutions still have an important role.

intersecting-oppressions.reason: Race, sex and class often interact in people's lives, so policies that ignore those overlaps tend to miss important problems.

gender-identity-recognition.reason: I see real and reasonable disagreement about how legal gender categories should balance dignity against other protections.

assisted-dying.reason: Competent terminally ill adults should have strong safeguards and a legal option to end suffering on their own terms.

left-right-obsolete.reason: The labels blur in practice, but the underlying disagreements about equality and markets still divide people.

alienated-labor.reason: Many wage jobs do cut people off from the meaning and creativity of their work, though not only under capitalism.

islam-incompatible.reason: Muslims live fully within Western societies and their values overlap with the broader liberal tradition, so the claim of basic incompatibility is wrong.

divine-source-of-authority.reason: I think political authority rests on the consent and accountability of the governed rather than on divine appointment.

religious-dress-in-state.reason: Neutrality in state roles has merit, but so does allowing people to express their faith, and the balance depends on context.

ban-nda-harassment.reason: Secret settlements that hide harassment protect abusers, so workers should be able to take those complaints to court.

social-market-economy.reason: Competitive markets work best with rules against monopoly and a safety net for people who lose out.

abolish-armed-forces.reason: A country without any defence capacity would be vulnerable, even if military spending deserves scrutiny.

rich-first.reason: Accepting that some are left behind during growth tends to entrench inequality that is hard to undo later.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.reason: Neutrality protects a country from entanglement, while alliances offer security, and the best choice depends on circumstances.

dynastic-succession.reason: Heads of state should be chosen through election or merit, not inherited within a family.

interest-free-mutual-credit.reason: User-owned banks are a sound model in some settings, but I am not confident they would work better than ordinary regulated banking overall.

refuse-lender-austerity.reason: Lenders can reasonably attach conditions, but some austerity demands have caused avoidable harm, so I weigh each case.

property-franchise.reason: Tying the vote to wealth denies political equality to ordinary citizens who are full members of the country.

domination-women-nature.reason: Some thinkers find a shared logic of domination in both, but I am not convinced the causes are as tightly linked as the claim says.

reification.reason: Market forces do shape how people see their relationships, though I doubt markets are as thoroughly disguising as the claim suggests.

press-owned-by-wealth.reason: Concentrated ownership of media and venues does limit whose voices are heard, even though those freedoms still matter.

promulgated-standing-laws.reason: Governing by published general laws applied by independent courts is one of the most important safeguards against arbitrary power.

racial-franchise.reason: Limiting the vote and office to one racial or ethnic group is a plain denial of equal citizenship.

online-participation.reason: Online deliberation can widen participation, but it also invites manipulation and polarisation, so I am torn.

open-government-data.reason: Publishing decision records and how proposals were handled makes government accountable and checkable.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.reason: Adults should be free to marry across religious lines, and the state should not restrict it.

boycott-minority-shops.reason: Deliberately shunning shops because of their owners' religion is discrimination.

citizens-assembly.reason: Randomly chosen citizens deliberating on hard questions can produce thoughtful results, though they need expert support and clear limits.

reinterpret-religion.reason: Religious traditions have always reinterpreted doctrine, but whether and how to do so is for believers to decide, so I am torn.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.reason: Extreme concentrations of money can translate into political influence, so limiting them helps protect equal liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.reason: Sexual orientation has no bearing on ability to serve, so gay and lesbian people should serve openly.

state-promotes-atheism.reason: A state should stay neutral on belief, so promoting unbelief through public schools is a mistake.

abolish-police-prisons.reason: Some form of policing and prisons is needed to protect people, though they should be far more humane and reformed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.reason: Guaranteed power-sharing can keep deeply divided societies peaceful, but it can also entrench divisions, so I am torn.

charity-over-state-aid.reason: Local charities and communities add real value, but large public programs are needed for reliable coverage, so I am torn.

term-limits.reason: Term limits bring turnover, but they also cost voters a choice and lose experience, so I am torn.

vote-delegation.reason: Revocable delegation is an interesting idea, but it adds complexity and concentrates influence in intermediaries, so I am torn.

existential-risk-priority.reason: Catastrophic risks deserve serious attention, though they should be weighed against pressing present harms.

women-in-religious-leadership.reason: Women's equal eligibility for religious office is a fair principle, even though religious communities should decide their own practice.

shared-marital-authority.reason: Spouses are equal partners, so authority within a marriage should be shared rather than held by one.

foreign-residents-local-vote.reason: Long-term residents who live under local rules can reasonably have a voice in local elections.

rent-control.reason: Caps can protect tenants in shortages but can also reduce supply and upkeep, so the evidence leaves me torn.

abolish-ip.reason: Some legal protection for inventors and creators helps fund new work, though the current term lengths are often too long.

uniformed-youth.reason: Young people's associations should be free and voluntary rather than drilled for national ends.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.reason: The arguments against hosting nuclear weapons are strong, but so are the security arguments for them, so I am torn.

no-foreign-bases.reason: Sovereignty matters, but allied bases can also bring real security, so the answer depends on the specific case.

recognise-genocide.reason: Officially acknowledging genocide is part of honest historical accountability, though labels are best left to careful scholarship.

income-for-work-not-ownership.reason: Pay for work matters, but returns on capital and property are also a legitimate part of a market economy, so I am torn.

never-kill-self-defence.reason: Lethal force is sometimes the only way to stop a deadly attack, so an absolute prohibition seems too strong.

unbroken-national-continuity.reason: Nations change a great deal over time, so claiming an unbroken identity from antiquity overstates continuity.

sex-socially-constructed.reason: Sex is a biological fact, while gender roles and categories are where culture and language do most of their shaping.

no-fixed-category-of-women.reason: Women differ widely, but a shared interest in equality still gives feminist politics a common ground, so I am torn.

martyrs-honoured.reason: Honouring the national dead is reasonable, but calling them saints turns civic remembrance into something sacred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.reason: Politics is mainly about interests, institutions and compromise, not a cosmic battle between good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.reason: A homeland can inspire a diaspora without holding everyone, but the right balance depends on circumstances, so I am torn.

culture-before-state.reason: Cultures and states shape each other, so making cultural renewal wait for statehood seems the wrong order.

god-not-male.reason: Religious language is a matter for believers and their traditions, so I decline to weigh in strongly.

scripture-judged-by-women.reason: Judging teachings by their effect on women's dignity is a serious moral test, but applying it to scripture is for believers, so I am torn.

economy-in-majority-hands.reason: Economic life should be open to everyone regardless of group, so reserving it for the majority is discrimination.

single-unit-for-people.reason: Giving a people its own region can be just, but borders that follow ethnicity can also create new minorities, so I am torn.

independent-unions.reason: Unions do their job best when they answer to their members rather than to the state or a party.

socialism-needs-workers-power.reason: Real worker power is central to what socialism promises, so state ownership alone seems not enough.

local-essentials-public.reason: Water, hospitals and local transport are essentials that public ownership can protect, though contracting can work well too.

second-chamber.reason: A second chamber adds checks but also delay and cost, so reasonable systems differ and I am torn.

municipal-property.reason: Local ownership of productive assets has real appeal, but private and state ownership each have strengths, so I am torn.

confederal-coordination.reason: Local assemblies with coordinating councils is an appealing design, but binding joint decisions are often needed, so I am torn.

family-wage.reason: Pay that can support a household is a fair goal for work, though pay should also track the value of the job.

ageing-research-funding.reason: Research into healthy ageing is valuable, though it should be weighed against other health priorities.

anonymous-payments.reason: Financial privacy protects people, but it also helps crime and evades law, so I am torn.

online-anonymity.reason: Pseudonymity protects people from harassment and surveillance, though accountability for abuse still matters.

person-over-state.reason: Individuals have a dignity that the state and community may not override for their own ends.

spiritual-nature.reason: Meaning and spirit matter alongside material needs, though politics should mainly address material conditions.

regional-powers-revocable.reason: Regional powers should rest on constitutional guarantees rather than on the national legislature's discretion.

gm-crops.reason: Gene editing can raise yields with fewer inputs, though each product still needs careful safety review.

dense-cities.reason: Compact development generally uses less energy and land per person than sprawl.

racial-group-interests.reason: Organising politics around race entrenches division and is a poor basis for political interests.

racial-pride.reason: Pride in heritage and ancestry is fine, though it is different from ranking races.

defensive-wars-only.reason: A strict defence-only rule is too narrow, since collective security and humanitarian missions can be legitimate.

language-defines-nation.reason: Language and history matter, but a nation should be defined by what its people choose, not by language alone.

communal-electorates.reason: Separate communal electorates entrench divisions; common electorates are better for a shared civic life.

foreign-partition-plot.reason: Outside interference happens, but a sweeping claim of a plot to partition the country needs evidence.

free-public-college.reason: Free tuition has real benefits, but it involves trade-offs in funding and targeting that leave me torn.

pollution-taxes.reason: Pricing pollution is an efficient tool, though regulation is often needed alongside it.

future-generations.reason: We have real obligations to future people to avoid damaging the environment we pass on.

women-distinct-values.reason: Attributing care and nonviolence to women as a group is a stereotype, and weighting views by sex is not sound.

arms-reduction.reason: Keeping armaments to what security requires is sensible, though the right level depends on context.

open-diplomacy.reason: Public treaties strengthen accountability, though some confidentiality in negotiations is practically necessary.

capital-controls.reason: Capital controls can help in crises but carry costs, so I am torn.

state-arms-monopoly.reason: A state monopoly on legitimate force is a sound basis, with legitimate resistance forces as a context-dependent exception.

soldiers-refuse-war.reason: Conscience matters and unlawful orders may be refused, but a general duty to refuse lawful orders undermines military order.

collective-bargaining.reason: Sector-wide bargaining gives workers real leverage and produces fair common rules.

in-work-tax-credits.reason: Tax credits for low-paid working families are an effective way to support work and reduce poverty.

fiscal-rules-binding.reason: Fiscal rules discipline borrowing, though rigid rules can backfire in downturns.

restructure-world-economy.reason: The international economic system has real imbalances that disadvantage poorer countries.

smash-state-machine.reason: Wholesale destruction of existing institutions is usually more harmful than reforming and making them accountable.

free-economic-experiment.reason: Pluralism in economic arrangements is attractive, though some shared rules are still needed.

nature-as-capital.reason: Accounting for natural capital helps, but not all of nature's value can or should be captured in prices.

sacred-nation.reason: Nations are real and meaningful, but calling them sacred overstates the case.

student-debt-relief.reason: There are fair arguments on both sides about borrowers' responsibility and public benefit, so I am torn.

internal-colonialism.reason: The analogy captures real regional inequalities, but it is a loose comparison, so I am torn.

shared-human-nature.reason: A shared human nature grounds dignity and rights, though its exact content is debated.

public-service-media.reason: Independent public broadcasting supports a healthy news system.

religions-one-truth.reason: Religions make incompatible claims, and the view that they share one truth is appealing but not demonstrable.

farm-price-support.reason: Price floors and public support protect farmers but distort markets, so I am torn.

keep-nuclear-weapons.reason: Unilateral disarmament carries risk, but keeping arsenals carries grave risks too; multilateral disarmament is preferable.

workers-own-party.reason: Labour parties have strong records, but broad parties also represent workers, so I am torn.

women-property-inheritance.reason: Women should have the same legal rights as men to inherit and own land.

one-language-many-names.reason: Where the line between language and dialect falls is genuinely contested, so I am torn.

pollution-tort-liability.reason: Regulatory agencies generally handle pollution better than scattered lawsuits, though liability should complement them.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.reason: Consulting traditional leaders can be valuable, but formal law-making roles raise legitimacy questions, so I am torn.

environment-over-liberty.reason: Environmental protection matters, but individual liberty should not be routinely subordinated to it.

mandatory-sentences.reason: Mandatory minimums reduce judicial discretion in ways that can produce unjust results.

immigrants-learn-language.reason: Language skills help integration, and a requirement backed by support is reasonable.

no-compulsory-union.reason: Voluntary membership and fair representation pull in different directions, so I am torn.

voter-id.reason: ID requirements help election integrity but can burden eligible voters, so the design matters and I am torn.

religious-equal-recognition.reason: Equal treatment by the state of different religious interpretations is a sound principle.

democracy-is-procedure.reason: Free elections are necessary for democracy, but democracy also requires rights and real popular rule.

premarital-sex.reason: Adults should decide their own sexual relationships, with no moral censure for women specifically.

internet-shutdowns.reason: Shutdowns cause significant harm and are rarely proportionate to the problem they address.

negative-income-tax.reason: Merging welfare into one cash payment has appeal but real design risks, so I am torn.

women-suffrage.reason: Women should vote and hold public office on the same terms as men.

religion-oppresses-women.reason: Religious law and teaching have often justified limiting women, though the effect varies widely by tradition and place.

race-social-construct.reason: Racial categories were largely drawn by people, though human population differences in genetics are real and gradual.

gender-equality-agencies.reason: Dedicated bodies can keep gender equality on the government's agenda, provided they are given real powers.

homestead-ownership.reason: First appropriation can ground a claim, but it does not settle ownership on its own without limits on what is taken.

international-criminal-courts.reason: Leaders who order aggression or mass atrocities should be answerable to courts that stand above their own state.

scripture-inerrant.reason: I do not think a sacred text is free of human authorship and error, so I cannot hold it inerrant in the literal sense.

gendered-self-government.reason: Self-rule that leaves out women's equal say risks entrenching exclusion, so equality is worth securing from the start.

defend-planned-state.reason: What such a state does for its people matters more than its ownership form, so I cannot endorse defending it regardless of its rulers.

indirect-election.reason: Delegate systems can be workable and sometimes more deliberate, but direct votes are usually more accountable.

national-church-status.reason: I think the state should treat religious bodies equally rather than privilege one in law.

minority-territorial-autonomy.reason: Where a minority is a local majority, letting it govern much of its own affairs is a reasonable way to respect it.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.reason: A local vote can give a real voice to residents, but it can also be manipulated or ignore the wider claims involved.

keep-colonial-borders.reason: Redrawing borders after independence would invite more conflict than it would solve, so keeping them is the safer principle.

simple-living.reason: Living with modest needs has real merit, but making it the general standard for everyone seems too restrictive.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.reason: Protecting an indigenous majority's land and culture matters, but restricting where citizens may live is a costly limit on freedom.

equal-conscription.reason: If a state drafts people, it should not split the obligation by sex without a strong reason.

homeland-spiritual-bond.reason: Attachment to ancestral land is meaningful to many people, but treating it as a duty that defines the nation is a contestable claim.

extrajudicial-killing.reason: Killing suspects without a trial removes due process and invites abuse, whatever the drug crime involved.

close-ties-china.reason: Trade and diplomacy should follow a country's interests case by case, and I do not think the general lean is for me to set.

protect-kin-minorities.reason: States may reasonably support co-nationals abroad, but doing so can stoke tension with the countries where they live.

resources-common-ownership.reason: Private claims to land and resources can reasonably be paired with a share of their value owed to others.

self-ownership.reason: A person's body and labour should not be taken for others' ends without consent, though some limits for shared needs are defensible.

cut-consumption-tax.reason: Sales taxes on basics fall hardest on the poor, but they also raise steady revenue and can be offset in other ways.

targeted-social-spending.reason: Means-tested aid reaches those in greatest need, while universal services are simpler and build broader support.

bypass-parties-groups.reason: Parties and organised groups let citizens aggregate their views and hold leaders to account, so bypassing them weakens representation.

no-business-privileges.reason: Special deals for firms close to government invite corruption, so equal treatment is the better default.

no-denominational-politics.reason: Organising politics around religious denominations tends to entrench divisions, so cross-cutting parties are preferable.

tech-with-ancestral-values.reason: Some blend of technology and inherited values is possible, but which values should lead is a judgment I hold loosely.

wife-divorce-without-consent.reason: A spouse should not be trapped in a marriage by the other's refusal to consent to ending it.

national-resource-control.reason: A country should generally have the final say over the wealth beneath its land, though foreign investment can still bring benefits.

distribution-by-process.reason: How wealth was obtained matters, but a very unequal outcome can still be unjust even when every step was voluntary.

financial-transactions-tax.reason: A small levy on currency and financial trades could damp speculation and raise revenue with limited cost to ordinary trade.

racism-not-main-obstacle.reason: Structural and interpersonal racism still shape outcomes for disadvantaged groups, so I would not call it no longer a main obstacle.

unjust-law-not-binding.reason: Gross injustice can rightly strain a person's duty to obey, but calling such a law not law at all is a contested step.

automate-paid-work.reason: Automation can free people from drudgery, but the pace and who benefits are questions that depend on institutions.

multipolar-world.reason: A balance among several strong centres can reduce the risk of one power dominating, though it brings its own rivalries.

labour-theory-of-value.reason: Prices reflect demand, scarcity and many inputs, so labour alone does not determine value.

patriotism-serves-workers.reason: Attachment to one's country and solidarity with working people can coexist, and often reinforce each other.

material-over-identity.reason: Economic interests are central for workers, but cultural recognition also matters, and the two can be pursued together.

market-under-party-rule.reason: Some one-party states have run market sectors, but whether that counts as socialism is a matter of definition and debate.
